description: This course traces the development of phenomenology from G.W.F. Hegel through Edmund Husserl and into its existential and critical transformations in Edith Stein, Martin Heidegger, and Simone de Beauvoir, among others. The course introduces core phenomenological concepts such as intentionality, the phenomenological method, and the constitution of meaning. Topics include selfhood, freedom, being-in-the-world, intersubjectivity, and the phenomenology of gender. Prerequisites: two courses in philosophy, one of which must be either PHIL 235 or PHIL 236 or permission of the department chair.
fullname: Seminar in the History of Philosophy
